holidays.name: CD Player Day
holidays.description: Dust off the jewel cases and hit play. This day salutes the shiny little machine that made scratchy vinyl crackle and tape hiss feel old-fashioned. Spin a favorite album from start to finish and enjoy the crisp, skip-free sound.
holidays.origin: The date marks the October 1, 1982 launch of the Sony CDP-101 in Japan, the first commercially available compact disc player.
holidays.funFact: The CDP-101 launched alongside a small catalog of titles, and Billy Joel's 52nd Street was one of the first albums released on CD.

holidays.name: Willy Wonka Day
holidays.description: A day for pure imagination. Fans of the candy-making genius celebrate with chocolate, golden-ticket daydreams, and a movie marathon of Wonka adventures. Everlasting gobstoppers are optional, but sweets are strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial pop-culture observance inspired by Roald Dahl's beloved Charlie and the Chocolate Factory and its film adaptations.
holidays.funFact: Roald Dahl's book was published in 1964, and in early drafts Charlie was reportedly a different character, with a much longer list of naughty children.

holidays.name: International Raccoon Appreciation Day
holidays.description: Give a nod to the masked bandit of the backyard. Raccoons are clever, dexterous, and famously fond of raiding garbage cans. Today is for admiring their cunning, from opening latches to dunking snacks in water.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, celebrated by wildlife fans and trash-panda enthusiasts.
holidays.funFact: A raccoon's front paws are so sensitive that they get much of their sense of touch information from them, and the famous 'washing' of food is thought to heighten that sense.
